digest.component_or_area: Development process and quality metrics infrastructure
propositions: True escaped-defect measurement is unavailable: only 7 of 648 bugs have detected_by metadata (1.1% coverage), preventing calculation of bug-escape rate or detection-stage efficiency.

Defect attribution via caused_by links is advisory and noisy: 39 source tickets linked to 49 bugs, with larger diffs increasing blame-attribution likelihood, and the top 8-bug fan-in source demonstrating semantic false-positive risk.

Plan review churned repeatedly: first-pass rate 49.0% with p90 attempts 8, consuming 116,560 LLM calls across 4,530 results; review-before-claim adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2) to 79.5% (Q3), but causal quality impact is not separated from process maturation.

Code-review first-pass is 97.4% (1,178 of 1,209 changes), but this describes funnel passage, not reviewer effectiveness or escape prevention; Gerrit reviewer/vote independence and force-bypass governance were not audited.

Code-health debt pressure exists: 35 modules at or above 720 LOC (15 above 780), 4.09% duplication, and same-file retouch 47.7% of consecutive pairs suggest hotspots; process maturation shows smaller source diffs (median 95 vs 111.5 lines Q3 vs Q2) and increased test co-change.

OSS governance baseline is strong (ticket trailers, DCO, Change-Id ~100% August adoption, commits 0%/0%/0% to 90.4%/82.9%/99.3% Q2–Q3), but authorship is concentrated (top operator/bot 92.4% of commits) and independent human-review rotation or external-contributor time-to-merge were not measured.
